runtime.execution: Host JS event loop, async row/cell generators and pluggable sources/UDFs.
runtime.service_boundary: A read/query composition library over supplied data; not a standing storage engine or agent.

summary: Lazy cell materialization makes expensive API/model calls query demand-driven; strong idea independent of its JS runtime.

inspection.scope: Read public exports, SQL normalization/planning/scan/abort path, UDF dispatch, collect and expensive-cell/abort tests.
inspection.limits: No full SQL conformance or join/window algorithm audit; no persistent DB, agent scheduling or original audit supplied.

actions.name: executeSql / executePlan
actions.input: SQL/plan, tables, asynchronous functions and AbortSignal
actions.output: QueryResults with columns and async rows/cells
actions.lifecycle: Demand-driven stream; interruption can expose partial values plus error.

actions.name: collect
actions.lifecycle: Collects rows then evaluates cells concurrently; may consume substantial memory.

actions.name: UDF apply / data-source scan
actions.input: Evaluated SQL arguments or pushdown hints/signal
actions.output: Awaited scalar or async scan rows
actions.lifecycle: Caller-defined IO lifetime and side effects.

evidence.claim: SQL executes over supplied tables/functions/signal and returns planned lazy results; host event-loop yield interval is 4000.
Scan receives pushdown hints/signal, invalid partial pushdown errors and cooperative abort is surfaced after scan completion.
User-defined functions are awaited after case-insensitive name lookup.
collect first gathers rows then materializes cells concurrently; stream interface avoids whole-result collection.
Documented scope is streaming async read-only SQL and lazy async cells, not storage durability.
Call-count assertions distinguish zero unselected work from selected/filter/limit-driven expensive calls.

tests.oracle: Counters expect zero for unselected columns and exact 1/2/5 demand-dependent calls; not cost/latency benchmark.
Rejects with aborted error; exactly Alice/Bob and two produced rows remain when aborted after second row.

strengths: Lazy structured queries can orchestrate expensive computations while avoiding unused work.
Abort surfaces truncation rather than silently treating partial scan as success.
limits: JS event-loop dependency conflicts with core preference; mechanism study does not select this library.
No durable storage or agent action lifecycle supplied.
arconaut_questions: Can a standing evidence/query interface lazily call remote computation without obscuring cost, identity and cancellation?
How is partial streamed data represented separately from completed query success?
